name: Something in the Eaves
setup: You did not see it arrive. That is the whole of the problem — a Quickwood greatcat picks its moment first and reveals itself second, and it has already picked.

opponent.name: a Quickwood greatcat
opponent._poolsDerived_20260905: health removed: it was on the retired 3-7 scale and overrode a live synthesised sheet, which made a bout end in a median of ONE turn. The pool now derives from standing (30 + 5/level) through the level the threat implies. `yieldAtFraction` replaces an absolute `yieldAt` because a ratio is scale-free.

lethalNote: Erik's ruling 2026-07-19: wild animals are lethal — they are. Defeat here is not incapacitation. The stakes dial (SNG-170) governs whether a profile meets them at all, not whether a boar can kill.

party.ifYouBringPeople: ⛔ *TAKES-THE-SLOWER-ONE*. Its tactic tag is already a party tag and nobody noticed — ⚠️ with one person it means you; WITH THREE IT MEANS YOUR SLOWEST, and it was behind them before the scene started.
party.whatItAsksOfAParty: ⛔ Whether you know who your slowest is. ⚑ The cell selects a party member FOR you, and travelling with someone slower is the whole risk.
party.foldNote: ⚠️ A folded KNOW ally answers *was-already-behind-you*. ⛔ Nothing else does.

_partyClauseWhy: ⛔ THE PARTY CLAUSE — R36/R36a, authored 2026-09-05. Every encounter in the corpus was written when a fight was ONE PERSON AGAINST ONE OPPONENT. ⚑ R36 makes a party member fight from their own sheet; R36a caps three acting fully and folds the rest. ⚠️ THE CLAUSE IS ADDITIVE — no prose changed. It is what a GM reads when more than one person is present.
